owner_instruction: All ACTUALLY running agents D/A/M/W/S/G/H should understand and use these network ranges correctly when a legitimate authenticated service requires a Render outbound source-IP allowlist; this is not an instruction to enumerate/scan hosts.
network_type: Shared Render-hosting IP ranges; use as potential outbound egress source-IP CIDRs, not as direct service destinations or guaranteed static IPs for an individual agent.
important_notes: Each /24 covers 256 addresses; the two ranges together cover 512 IP addresses. No individual destination services or ports were supplied.
These CIDR blocks do not create AI instances, establish model connections, grant agent access, or fix any Render deployment failures.
Before authorizing traffic by source IP, check that the service's Render Dashboard -> Connect -> Outbound list actually includes these ranges for that deployed service and region.
Shared source IP address ranges can include other customers; allowlisting must be paired with normal strong authentication.
Run automated jobs against explicitly authorized HTTPS URLs or documented APIs only; do not ping, sweep, enumerate, port-scan, exploit, or brute-force the CIDRs.

Each actually executed agent should document the intended provider, approved destination hostname, request type, source evidence, outcome/status, and any limitations. Do not claim a connection without logs.
No charges, credentials, private keys or paid outbound routing are authorized by this instruction.
agent_action: If a legitimate external API explicitly requires source-IP allowlisting, explain these owner-provided Render CIDRs and verify the specific deployed service's current outbound ranges. Work on permitted source-specific research rather than bulk probing.
